newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway welcomes Israeli-PLO Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Norway welcomes Israeli-PLO Hebron deal.

text.p: Norway, mediator of the Israeli-Palestinian peace accords, on Wednesday welcomed an agreement to extend Palestinian rule to Hebron in the West Bank.
"We are very happy that Israel and the PLO have now agreed on a solution in Hebron," Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal said in a statement.
"At the same time I wish to praise the United States for its active participation in the negotiations," he said.
Godal said Norway, which brokered the historic 1993 Israeli-PLO peace pact, hoped that the peace process after considerable delay would now gain momentum again.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat sealed the U.S.-brokered accord at a late-night summit and agreed on a timeframe for further Israeli pullbacks in the West Bank.
Godal noted that Norway's observers in Hebron would now be joined by observers from other nations, contributing to stability following the redeployment.

Hebron, a West Bank flashpoint, is home to 400 militant Jewish settlers and 100,000 Arabs. It was due to be given self-rule 10 months ago but violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June delayed the pullback.
